title: Near-Memory LLM Inference Processor based on 3D DRAM-to-logic Hybrid Bonding
problem: LLM inference requires both high memory bandwidth and substantial compute resources; traditional architectures separate memory from compute, creating bandwidth bottlenecks and energy inefficiency.
motivation: Near-memory computing via 3D DRAM-to-logic hybrid bonding enables massive parallelism and bandwidth, but prior designs suffer from distributed controller overhead and limited reconfigurability.
method: Proposed architecture uses centralized controller and dual-IO scheme on 3D DRAM-to-logic hybrid-bonded stack. Centralized control reduces area overhead and enables reconfigurable GEMV/GEMM operations, adapting to inference phases.
key_novelty: Centralized controller with dual-IO on 3D hybrid-bonded DRAM enables efficient, reconfigurable LLM inference without distributed controller overhead.
contributions: Centralized controller design reducing chip area overhead
Dual-IO scheme enabling reconfigurable GEMV/GEMM operations
2.9x-3.5x performance improvement over NPU and DRAM-PIM baselines for OPT 66B

metrics.speedup: 2.9x vs NPU, 3.5x vs DRAM-PIM, 2.5x vs heterogeneous (DRAM-PIM + NPU)

primary_theme: Near-memory LLM inference via centralized-controller 3D hybrid bonding
